host.provenance: the Node 16 runtime the Angular verticals already materialised under <REPO>/.versionless/cache; not re-acquired by this spike
host.satisfiesDeclaredEngines: Angular 12 declares node ^12.14.1 || >=14.0.0 and Angular 13 declares ^12.20.0 || ^14.15.0 || >=16.10.0; 16.20.2 satisfies both

scratchRoot: <REPO>/.versionless/work/spike-ngcc-1213 (unversioned scratch; nothing under it is committed)
method: three minimal closures, npm install --legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund, then (1) targeted ngcc per library, (2) full ngcc over the closure, (3) an AOT consumption probe: one NgModule importing all three library NgModules plus a component whose template instantiates one element from each library, compiled with ngc -p tsconfig.probe.json under fullTemplateTypeCheck.

a13rx6.rationale: Angular 13.4.0 peer-declares rxjs ^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0, so rxjs 6 at Angular 13 is a legal closure. This closure isolates whether the a13 failure is an Angular-13 property or an rxjs-7 property.

typesPinNote: @types/leaflet and @types/geojson are floating ranges in @yaga/leaflet-ng2's own dependencies. Left to float they resolve to versions whose syntax TypeScript 4.3/4.6 cannot parse, and the probe drowns in TS1005/TS1109 parse errors from a transitive typing package. Pinning them to the era (1.7.11 / 7946.0.8) removes that noise entirely. This is a real cell hazard, and it is not a pre-Ivy hazard.

nonclaims: No application was migrated, built or run. These are compiler readings over minimal synthetic closures, not a pigallery2 build, and they do not weaken the sealed pigallery2 RED, which stands as permanent falsification evidence at the Angular 16 cell.

The probe compiles one NgModule and one component template. It establishes that these three libraries are consumable by the Angular 12 and Angular 13 compilers; it establishes nothing about pigallery2 as a whole, whose migrated tree carries hundreds of other files and four still-open compile-stage demands.
Nothing was executed in a browser. No behavioural claim is made about the map, the switch or the loading bar at runtime.
No Angular 16 package was installed. The stub-ngcc reading at 16 is carried from the sealed record, not re-measured here.
Only Node 16.20.2 was available on this host. Nothing here establishes what these lines do under Node 12 or 14.

The Angular 13 green is conditional on rxjs 6. Nothing here establishes that pigallery2's own code runs on rxjs 6 at Angular 13; it establishes only that the closure is legal under Angular 13's declared peer range and that ngcc then succeeds.
The -p module main override was applied by hand at the command line. Nothing here establishes that the Angular CLI builder can be made to pass it, which is named as the first open question.
